title: Pulmonary fibrosis, scleroderma lung, tracheostomy and ventilator
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's lung fibrosis or airway status.
note:
Chief Complaint
Shortness of breath.

HPI
Pt is an 80 y.o. female presenting for f/u of respiratory symptoms. Pt reports progressive dyspnea on exertion over the last 3 months. She notes she is now unable to walk more than one block without stopping to rest. Denies acute chest pain, productive cough, or fevers. Pt states she has felt more fatigued lately. She reports a dry, non-productive cough that is worse at night. No recent travel or exposure to environmental irritants reported.

Review of Systems
Constitutional: Fatigue. Respiratory: Dyspnea on exertion, dry cough. Cardiovascular: No chest pain, no palpitations. MSK: No joint pain. Neuro: No dizziness, no focal weakness. GI: No changes in bowel habits.

Social History
Retired. Lives in a single-story home with her daughter. Non-smoker. Denies alcohol or illicit drug use.

Family History
Mother: Hypertension, age 85.
Father: Type 2 Diabetes, age 78.

Vitals
BP: 132/78
HR: 74 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 94% on RA
Ht: 12.2
Weight: 145 lbs

Recent Labs
CBC: WNL
BMP: Na 138, K 4.1, Cr 1.1, eGFR 72
Chest CT: Imaging reveals interstitial changes consistent with pulmonary fibrosis. The etiology of the pulmonary fibrosis is not determined.

Medication List
Lisinopril 10mg daily
Atorvastatin 20mg daily
Multivitamin daily

Exam
General: Alert and oriented x3. Appears in no acute distress.
Respiratory: CTAB. Breath sounds diminished in bilateral bases. No wheezes or crackles noted on auscultation.
Cardiovascular: RRR, S1, S2. No murmurs.
Musculoskeletal: Normal gait.
Skin: No rashes or lesions.

Assessment
1. Pulmonary fibrosis: Imaging shows pulmonary fibrosis; however, the specific cause is not determined at this time. Pt is symptomatic with exertional dyspnea.

Plan
1. Pulmonology Referral: Place referral to pulmonology for further evaluation of pulmonary fibrosis and diagnostic workup.
2. Follow-up: Pt to f/u in clinic after pulmonology evaluation.
3. Education: Discussed symptoms and importance of specialist follow-up.

Electronically signed, T. Haddad, NP, 05/14/2026
explanations: Pulmonary fibrosis without a documented cause: J84.10 (HCC 280).
